description: Systematic comparison of all lower bound approaches for γ₂

approaches.name: Frog Dynamics (Periodic Word Optimization)
approaches.method: MC estimation of γ(W) = E[LCS(W^(n), Random)]/n for periodic binary words
approaches.computational_cost: O(n²) per trial via C-accelerated DP
approaches.notes: Valid lower bound (γ₂ ≥ γ(W) for all W). Weaker than Heineman's DFA bound but provides independent confirmation.

approaches.name: Heineman et al. 2024 (Literature SOTA)
approaches.method: DFA with h=14 and optimized LP certificate on ~268M states
approaches.notes: Current best known rigorous lower bound

approaches.name: Lueker 2009 Lower Bound
approaches.method: DFA with h=11 and LP certificate

approaches.name: Online Matching (Greedy/Lookahead)
approaches.method: Simplified DFA: greedy and lookahead matching of streaming characters
approaches.notes: Valid lower bound but much weaker than full Lueker DFA method

approaches.name: Neural Certificate (Gradient Optimization)
approaches.method: Gradient descent on certificate vector u(x) for buffer matching model
approaches.notes: Failed: simplified buffer model does not encode subsequence ordering. Gradient optimization unable to find feasible certificates.

analysis.reasoning: The DFA-based approach (Heineman 2024) remains far superior because it leverages the full structure of the LCS DP recurrence through an exponential state space (4^h). Our online matching approximation loses subsequence ordering, and the neural certificate failed on the simplified model. Frog dynamics gives valid but weak bounds. For future improvement: either scale the full DFA method to h=15-16 (requiring ~4B states), or find a compact representation of the certificate vector that avoids the exponential blowup.
